title: agno ClickHouse vector store -- T1059 unsafe f-string metadata SQL injection in delete_by_metadata
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-10105 (CVSS 8.7 HIGH), a
self-reported issue for agno (2.6.5), an AI-agent framework, in its
ClickHouse vector-database backend.

`clickhousedb.py`'s `delete_by_metadata()` built its `WHERE` clause with
unsafe f-string interpolation of caller-supplied metadata keys and
values directly into the SQL text:
`f"JSONExtractString(toString(filters), '{key}') = '{value}'"`. Neither
`key` nor `value` was escaped or parameterized. An attacker who controls
either -- for example, metadata attached to agent-ingested content --
can supply a `value` like `1' OR '1'='1` to turn the intended equality
check into a tautology, producing
`JSONExtractString(toString(filters), 'user_id') = '1' OR '1'='1'` and
matching every row rather than the intended one: mass deletion, targeted
row deletion, or error-based/blind data extraction, per the advisory.

Detection logic flags the resulting query-log artifact: a
`JSONExtractString` predicate whose value operand contains a SQL
boolean-tautology or comment idiom (`' OR '`, `'='`, `--`, `/*`) rather
than an ordinary metadata value -- this is the specific function this
vulnerable code path builds, so its presence with an injection idiom is
a tight signal, not a generic "SQL keyword in a query" heuristic.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor disclosure (agno-agi, via the
linked issue and merged fix PR, corroborated by VulnCheck's independent
write-up), fixed via ClickHouse named-parameter binding (indexed
`meta_key_N`/`meta_val_N` parameters handled by the driver's own
escaping layer, matching the secure pattern already used elsewhere in
the same file).
